question: Can one route12/Budget16 V16 target step execute in at most 1.55 seconds while reproducing its frozen scalar trajectory and a state-sensitive continuation?
hardware: Lucebox4; gfx1151 target; single owner; build parallelism at most 4
protocol: Run scalar route12/Budget16 for 18 generated IDs and freeze that candidate trajectory.
Run one 16-row grouped target step over the first 16 candidate IDs, require all 16 argmax rows to match IDs 1 through 16, and commit all rows.
Run one scalar continuation from the committed state and require the next argmax to match candidate ID 17.
Require byte-identical final continuation logits versus the scalar control and identical logical policy inputs.
Report target-step wall separately from the untimed scientific interpretation; do not call the target-only oracle deployable throughput.

gate.go: target step <= 1.55 seconds, complete 16/16 trajectory agreement, continuation agreement, byte-identical continuation logits, no macro/provider failure, and valid telemetry
gate.promising_but_incomplete: target step > 1.55 and <= 1.75 seconds with all correctness gates; retain only as an optimization candidate
gate.no_go: target step > 1.75 seconds, any correctness failure, or any macro/provider runtime failure

scope: Research-only target ceiling. Registered exact-route fallback bytes remain part of the route12/Budget16 policy and must be reported; they are not a runtime failure. This is not native-exact K3, a real draft result, or production promotion.
